correctness.rationale: Every unordered pair has canonical circular coordinates P(r,x). The integer D=(r-1)n+n-x decreases by exactly one under a when x<n-1 and under b when x=n-1, while a complete case check shows neither generator can decrease D by more than one. Therefore any synchronizing word has length at least D. The explicit word a^(n-1-x)b(a^(n-1)b)^(r-1) has exactly length D and synchronizes the pair, proving equality. Converting the two possible orientations of {i,j} gives the stated minimum formula. Reverse-BFS verification independently matches the formula for every pair for 2<=n<=80.

originality.rationale: The direct source already proves the extremal value RDV(2,n)=binom(n,2), which immediately implies the unlabeled multiset of pair weights along a longest geodesic; that implication is explicitly credited and is not treated as new. The surviving claim is the state-resolved closed formula assigning the exact shortest synchronization time to every labeled pair. Searches under pair-weight, pair-automaton distance, exact-coordinate, average, and Černý aliases found no source stating or implying that assignment formula. The principal residual risk is Cardoso's 2014 thesis, whose repository metadata was accessible but whose full body was not obtained through the bounded public route.

value.rationale: Pair synchronization is the base layer of the rendezvous-time framework and the Černý family is the canonical extremal family. A state-resolved exact formula is a natural complete classification: it turns the known worst-case witness into a metric on every pair, gives explicit shortest-word lengths without search, and supplies a monotone rank coordinate useful for analyzing pair-layer dynamics. The claim is intentionally not inflated by treating the already implied unlabeled spectrum as new.
